page: Amazon Web Services g6f.4xlarge is a graphics-intensive virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 16 vCPUs, 8 physical cores, and a base clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The system is equipped with 64 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4 GB of RAM per core. For accelerated workloads, the instance includes a fractional NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering 11 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 450 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 10 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core tests, while multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench scores remain in the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests reveal a notable tradeoff: small-block cached read operations perform at average levels, but large-block uncached read and write operations are weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Conversely, the hardware excels in LLM inference prompt processing, achieving top-tier performance in the top 10% for small and medium models, and strong performance in the top 25% for large models. Text generation speeds for these models remain average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g6f.4xlarge offers a balanced resource density by bundling a fractional GPU with a solid mid-range CPU and local NVMe storage. This configuration avoids the higher expense of a full dedicated GPU when fractional acceleration is sufficient. The instance is well-suited for workloads such as low-latency LLM prompt processing, graphics rendering, media transcoding, and general-purpose applications requiring moderate GPU acceleration alongside local SSD storage.
